subject: Action: NovaBank EU→APAC transfer mapping and TIA scoping
messages:
From: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@novabank.com>
To: logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: data-privacy@novabank.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU→APAC transfers: SCC vs UK-IDTA applicability + TIA scope

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our privacy and ops teams have a couple of urgent clarifying asks before we can proceed to DPA redlines:

1) We see Redwood's standard DPA references both the EU SCCs and a UK IDTA/UK Addendum. For NovaBank's footprint (EU customers + customers in Singapore/HK), can you confirm the authoritative legal mechanism you plan to rely on for (a) EU data exported to Singapore and (b) UK-origin data routed to US infra?

2) Our InfoSec needs a concise TIA (Transfer Impact Assessment) scope: which subprocessors/processes are transient (JIT caching, CDNs, edge inference in APAC) vs persistent storage. We need to know whether any APAC subprocessors will be considered processors with access to customer content.

3) Attaching our current network/dataflow diagram — please annotate where Redwood's proposed safeguards apply. Also confirm whether your proposed fallback (onshore cache in EU) is documented in the DPA or handled operationally.

Can you loop in the right privacy contact and send an initial proposed TIA scope by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Luc
Head of Data Protection
NovaBank

---

From: logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
To: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@novabank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU→APAC transfers: SCC vs UK-IDTA applicability + TIA scope

Luc —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (Privacy & Legal liaison) and Naomi (Technical PM - infra) to draft an annotated mapping and an initial TIA scope.

Quick answers while we pull docs:
- Redwood's DPA supports both SCCs (standard transfers out of the EEA) and the UK Addendum/IDTA for UK-origin data; applicability depends on the origin and the contractual routing you choose.
- For transient edge inference (APAC), our standard approach is to treat those nodes as transient processors with ephemeral KV caches — they do not persist customer content beyond configured TTLs unless explicitly enabled.

We will: (a) annotate your diagram, (b) produce a one-page TIA scope that lists subprocessors and whether they are in-scope for the TIA, and (c) include proposed contractual language (DPA addendum) for onshore cache fallback. Expect a draft by Thu EOD (May 14).

— Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@novabank.com>, logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 13 May 2027 14:06:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU→APAC transfers: SCC vs UK-IDTA applicability + TIA scope

Luc / team —

Thanks — Kimberly here from Redwood's privacy team. Short version up front: we can support both legal mechanisms, but the controls and evidence we provide will differ. I outline concrete items below and attached a proposed TIA scope spreadsheet for your review.

Key points:
- Legal basis: For exports from EEA to Singapore, we propose SCCs plus organisational safeguards (contractual terms, encryption-in-transit, strict KV cache TTLs, audited access controls).
- UK-origin flows: if you have UK-resident data, our standard path is UK IDTA/UK Addendum to the SCCs (we'll include the addendum in the DPA package).
- Subprocessors: We operate a layered subprocessor model. For APAC edge inference we partner with a managed GPU provider (edge-gpu.apac.example) — classified as a transient processor (no persistent storage) unless you opt-in to onshore caching. If NovaBank requires onshore caching in Singapore, that subprocess will become in-scope for the TIA and will require additional attestations (encryption-at-rest, customer-specific key controls).

Ask from our side to finalize the TIA:
1) Please confirm which NovaBank data classes are considered personal data for this engagement (e.g., PII, account IDs, transaction metadata) and whether any fields must be redacted prior to inference.
2) Share any minimum retention TTLs or caching exceptions (if you require sub-second inference and longer TTLs, that affects the safeguard profile).
3) Provide a list of required evidence items (SOC2 report? penetration test? encryption key custody) — we can attach our standard packs but will surface gaps.

I have attached: proposed_tia_scope.xlsx (initial scoping for subprocessors and controls) and an annotated checklist. Also dropping a DocuSign link for an NDA addendum if needed.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_tia_scope.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet; 2 sheets: subprocessor_inventory, tia_controls_checklist)
Attachment: novabank-dataflow-diagram_v2.pdf (annotated request from Novabank)

From: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@novabank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU→APAC transfers: SCC vs UK-IDTA applicability + TIA scope

Kimberly — thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple clarifications from our privacy team inline:

> For APAC edge inference we partner with a managed GPU provider (edge-gpu.apac.example) — classified as a transient processor (no persistent storage) unless you opt-in to onshore caching.

If the APAC provider is truly transient, we are comfortable. However, two practical asks: (1) we require a process-level attestation that caches are purged on job completion and (2) we need to confirm whether any system-level logs (debugging traces, crash dumps) may contain snippets of customer content and where those logs are stored.

Also, for onshore cache fallback: if Redwood offers automatic fallback to an EU onshore cache when a preferred APAC node is unavailable, we need that documented in the DPA (so legal can see the contractual fallback route).

We confirm the data classes: PII (customer name, account id), transaction metadata (timestamps, merchant ids), and free-text messages (which may contain sensitive identifiers). We cannot agree to any persistent storage of free-text message content in APAC.

We'll sign the NDA addendum if needed. Please send the attestation language and the TIA draft as soon as it's ready.

Best,
Luc

---

From: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: Luc Moreau <luc.moreau@novabank.com>, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, logan_wright@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU→APAC transfers: SCC vs UK-IDTA applicability + TIA scope

Hi Luc — Naomi here. Technical follow-up and commitments from our infra team:

- Cache purge attestation: we will provide a canned attestation stating that ephemeral inference caches are purged at job completion and that TTLs are enforced. We will include log retention policies and redaction guidance.
- Crash/debug logging: by default, crash dumps are stored in our US logging cluster and never contain full request payloads; we will provide an extract of our logging architecture and a sample redaction filter. If NovaBank requires log residency or additional redaction, we can configure per-account redaction and routing (this is delivered as part of Redwood Private / Dedicated but available as an add-on for Hosted).
- Onshore cache fallback: feature exists and is operationally gated. Naomi action items: draft DPA clause for fallback (to be included in DPA addendum), produce the short TIA draft (1-2 pages) that enumerates subprocessors and transient vs persistent roles, and export the subprocessor attestations we have for edge-gpu.apac.example.

Next steps: Kimberly will circulate the TIA draft and legal language today; I will attach the infra attestation doc and the subprocessor certificate for edge-gpu.apac.example. Can we target a follow-up call Friday 09:00 BST to walk the TIA?

Thanks — Naomi
Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: edge-gpu-apac-attestation.pdf (attestation; 1 page)
